facts.statement: The only known species, P. wildi, is represented by two immature specimens, with the subadult reaching a length of 3 meters.
facts.quote: The type and only species is P. wildi, known from two immature specimens with the subadult measuring 3 m long.

facts.statement: The species Plesiopterys wildi was named by Frank Robin O'Keefe in 2004.
facts.quote: In 2004, Frank Robin O'Keefe named the species Plesiopterys wildi.

facts.statement: The specific name wildi honors German paleontologist Rupert Wild for his work on Mesozoic vertebrate paleobiology.
facts.quote: The specific name honors the German paleontologist Rupert Wild for his contributions to the Mesozoic vertebrate paleobiology in Germany.

facts.statement: The animal possessed 39 cervical vertebrae, with neck morphology more similar to Thalassiodracon than to Plesiosaurus.
facts.quote: Plesiopterys had 39 cervical vertebrae, with the neck having general morphology and proportions more similar to Thalassiodracon than to Plesiosaurus.

facts.statement: Evidence from a subadult specimen suggests plesiosaurs retained reptilian scaly skin, unlike some other Mesozoic marine reptiles.
facts.quote: This specimen suggests that plesiosaurs retained reptilian scaly skin unlike some Mesozoic marine reptiles like ichthyosaurs and metriorhynchids.

facts.statement: Researchers suggest the scales may have aided swimming or protected flippers during feeding on the seafloor.
facts.quote: The scales might have aided the plesiosaurs during swimming or protected the flippers during feeding on the seafloor.

facts.statement: The premaxilla bears four or five alveoli and five teeth, representing a primitive feature for plesiosaurs.
facts.quote: On the premaxilla, four or five alveoli are present, along with five premaxillary teeth, which is a plesiomorphic feature for plesiosaurs.

facts.statement: The mandible retains a prominent mandibular ridge, a feature lost in other plesiosaurids.
facts.quote: The mandible retains a prominent mandibular ridge, unlike the rest of plesiosaurids, which have lost the feature.

facts.statement: Phylogenetic analyses place Plesiopterys as a sister taxon to Franconiasaurus and the clade Cryptoclidia, more derived than Microcleididae.
facts.quote: Phylogenetic analyses have recovered Plesiopterys as a sister taxon of the genus Franconiasaurus and the clade Cryptoclidia, in a more derived position than the family Microcleididae.

facts.statement: Plesiopterys lived during the Toarcian stage, between 184.2 and 182.9 million years ago.
facts.quote: Time range: Toarcian to Toarcian (184.2 to 182.9 million years ago)

facts.statement: It is debated whether Plesiopterys is a distinct genus or a junior synonym of Seeleyosaurus guilelmiimperatoris, with recent studies arguing for its validity.
facts.quote: In 2007, Fransiska Großmann considered Plesiopterys a junior synonym of Seeleyosaurus guilelmiimperatoris. Sachs et al. (2025) has since interpreted Plesiopterys wildi as a taxon distinct from S. guilelmiimperatoris.
